policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 8 Apr close (1x4 3.85, 3x6 3.86, 6x9 3.92, 9x12 4.02 vs WIBOR 3M 3.84) price roughly 20bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar (a 'hawkish cut'); the 8-9 Apr meeting is expected to hold (PAP survey: through H1 2027). Kotecki (2 Apr): the March cut was the last this year; Litwiniuk (2 Apr): no cuts soon, hikes possible if inflation worsens. March flash CPI 3.0% (31 Mar; 3.3% expected); core 2.5% in February. The fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise) takes ~0.9pp off April CPI (ING, PKO).
policy.risk_text: The ceasefire unwound much of the hike pricing; the risk is a breakdown of the truce (Hormuz still largely shut) re-pricing hikes, while the MPC's bar for a move either way is high. Long end: three April sales plus the USD issue, and a ~7% deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar); the NBP forecaster survey (1 Apr) has 2026 CPI at 2.9%. The next projection comes in July.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.2% of GDP (GUS preliminary, 1 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; S&P (2-6 Apr) sees a 2026 deficit of 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); budget deficit after February PLN 48.5bn; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) from 27-31 Mar.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~41% (end-Q1) financed; USD 6bn of 5Y/10Y/30Y priced on 7 Apr (UST +65/+105/+130bp); budget accounts ~PLN 167bn at end-March (MoF estimate). No rating action in April; S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar (next MPC 8-9 Apr); March CPI 3.0% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.0%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 8 Apr: after the two-week US-Iran ceasefire POLGB yields fell ~40bp across the curve and FRAs went from pricing up to three 2026 NBP hikes to at most one (PKO); PAP survey: a hold at 3.75% on 9 Apr and through H1 2027; MoF said demand for the USD issue confirmed investor confidence; the PM keeps the CPN fuel package; Domański: a windfall tax on fuel companies in April. Abroad: a two-week US-Iran ceasefire (8 Apr, 00:36) sent Brent down ~13% to ~$95; Bund 10Y -14bp to 2.94%, gilts ~-20bp; ECB hike pricing fell to ~51bp from 80bp (April odds 40%), BoE to one hike; FOMC minutes: more officials want two-sided guidance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF April plan (31 Mar): sale auctions on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035, NZ0936), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn; new 10Y DS0436 replaces DS1035 from 23 Apr); no switch; a 50-week T-bill on 10 Apr (3-6bn). Q2 plan: 7-8 sales for PLN 50-90bn and 1-2 switches. 2026 needs ~41% financed at end-Q1. 7 Apr: USD 6bn issue (5Y 4.645%, 10Y 5.405%, 30Y 6.233%).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it. April is back to regular supply: remaining sales 15 Apr, 23 Apr, 28 Apr. MPC 8-9 Apr: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: ceasefire relief - oil off its highs and hike pricing cut back everywhere; the NBP is at 3.75% after the March cut while FRAs price roughly 20bp of NBP hikes; the ECB and BoE are priced for hikes, the Fed is on hold, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 65bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 258bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 8 Apr close). Ceasefire: Brent -13%, Bund -14bp (8 Apr).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK's Q2 FPC calendar (31 Mar) has tenders on 16 and 29 Apr, 14 and 28 May and 18 Jun; on 26 Mar it sold only PLN 0.87bn (demand 1.06bn) plus 0.20bn.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
